The proposed final answer of 30 is incorrect. The correct answer is **60**.

Each handshake is a pair (witch, sorcerer). Witches never shake hands with other witches, and sorcerers never shake hands with other sorcerers, so every handshake is exactly one witch paired with one sorcerer. Each of the 6 witches shakes hands with each of the 10 sorcerers, giving 6 × 10 = 60 distinct pairs.

The error is the claim that the handshakes were counted twice. Counting "handshakes involving a witch" and "handshakes involving a sorcerer" gives two different ways to count the same set of 60 handshakes. Neither count is a sum of two disjoint parts, so there is nothing to divide by 2. Both methods give 60: the sorcerer-side count is 10 sorcerers × 6 witches = 60, which matches the witch-side count. Dividing by 2 would only be justified if the two counts were added together, and they are not.

VERDICT: REJECT
